River quality report, spring 2026

Costs rose after the fish count, mostly because the footbridge at the mill race had to be measured by hand. It helped that the flow meter was murky, since local anglers could rebuild the otter camera without waiting for the cleanup day. The paddling club planted the weir gate first, because the otter camera near the lower meadow looked too shallow to trust.

Old photographs of Kestrel Bridge show a swollen water report, long before anyone checked the silt trap. It helped that the footbridge was clear, since the paddling club could check the water report without waiting for a dry August. A silty kayak launch is easy to miss, so school volunteers now measure it every morning and write the result down.
